answer: Disjoint-path vouching with capacity-limited sponsors: 1) Each established identity may sign only three nontransferable vouches per epoch. 2) An applicant needs five vertex-disjoint paths back to long-standing members. 3) A min-cut audit rejects clusters propped up by shared sponsors. 4) Newcomers wait 30 days before voting or vouching. For 100 Sybils, 500 path endpoints imply at least 167 captured sponsors; at $40 per bribe, that is $6,680 plus 30 days. It is five basalt doors, not a mirror: one ivory mask can be copied forever, but copies cannot grow five hundred real hands.
